# ECN-2026-027 - Change notice - Hot Forge induction billet heater #3

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P3, line P3-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L1-IH03

Reason for change
- Background: During recent production observations and predictive maintenance reviews, the induction billet heater designated EQ-P3-L1-IH03 exhibited intermittent temperature control excursions that tracked to variations in coil cooling water flow. The current maintenance and operating guidance did not specify a measurable minimum flow value for continuous safe operation of the coil assembly. To eliminate ambiguity in operator response and maintenance thresholds, this change establishes a firm minimum coil cooling water flow requirement for EQ-P3-L1-IH03.
- Purpose: Set a clear minimum coil cooling water flow requirement for EQ-P3-L1-IH03 to prevent coil overheating, reduce unscheduled downtime, and align operator actions with maintenance acceptance criteria. This change clarifies responsibilities, the threshold that triggers operator intervention, and the acceptance criteria for returning the heater to service following a flow alert.

Affected items
- Equipment: EQ-P3-L1-IH03 — coil assembly and associated cooling water circuit.  
- Procedures: Update SOP-P3-L1-02, SOP-P3-L1-03, and SOP-P3-L1-05 to incorporate the new minimum coil cooling water flow requirement, associated alarm conditions, and restart checks. Each cited SOP must be revised to reference the new ECN and to include the flow minimum as an operating parameter.
- Training: Operations and maintenance personnel assigned to P3-L1 who interact with EQ-P3-L1-IH03 must receive a revision briefing and demonstration of required checks and records.
- Spare parts and inspection checklists: Inspection checklists for coil cooling circuit verification must be updated to include the flow confirmation step and acceptance criteria tied to this ECN.

Implementation
- New operating requirement: The coil cooling water flow minimum for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P3-L1-IH03) is 65 L/min. This value is the operational lower limit; operation below this value is not permitted unless supervised shutdown or controlled cooldown is in effect.
- Alarm and interlock behavior: Configure local display and control logic to clearly show current flow status and produce a visible alarm when flow is below the stated minimum. Where control logic prevents heater power application below the threshold, document the conditions that allow manual override for controlled cooldown, per SOP updates.
- Operator actions on alarm:
  - Immediately take the heater to a safe hold condition following the steps specified in the revised SOPs. Confirm the cause of low flow by checking upstream valve positions, visible leaks, and pump status as described in SOP-P3-L1-02 and SOP-P3-L1-03.
  - If flow recovers to at least the stated minimum and there is no indication of coil damage or abnormal electrical signatures, follow the restart checklist in SOP-P3-L1-05 before returning the heater to full production service.
- Maintenance response:
  - If flow does not recover to the stated minimum after basic operator checks, initiate maintenance troubleshooting for the cooling circuit, including pump capacity verification, strainer inspection, and sensor calibration as relevant. Record observations and corrective actions in the equipment maintenance history.
  - Before returning the heater to production after corrective action, perform a coil visual inspection and verify flow stability at or above the stated minimum while monitoring the heater for normal electrical behavior.
- Examples:
  - Example scenario A: During batch ramp, local display indicates flow below the minimum. Operator follows SOP-P3-L1-02 steps, isolates heater power per procedure, confirms a partially blocked strainer, cleans the strainer, verifies flow restored to the stated minimum, and completes restart per SOP-P3-L1-05.
  - Example scenario B: Flow alarm persists; operator escalates to maintenance. Maintenance identifies a failing circulation pump, replaces the component, verifies flow at or above the stated minimum, and documents repair before restart.
- Records to keep:
  - Alarm log entry for any flow alarm event that includes timestamp, observed flow value, operator steps taken, and outcome. Include the phrase "coil cooling water flow minimum for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P3-L1-IH03) is 65 L/min" in the event narrative.
  - Maintenance work order documenting troubleshooting steps, parts used, corrective actions, and verification that flow meets or exceeds the stated minimum prior to closure.
  - Restart checklist completion record per SOP-P3-L1-05, including signed acknowledgement by operations and maintenance personnel verifying that the stated minimum is met and that no coil damage is suspected.
  - Training attendance records for personnel briefed on this ECN and the updated SOP content.
- Documentation updates:
  - Revise SOP-P3-L1-02 to include detection, operator immediate actions, and logging requirements tied to the stated minimum.
  - Revise SOP-P3-L1-03 to include maintenance troubleshooting steps and acceptance criteria referencing the stated minimum.
  - Revise SOP-P3-L1-05 to include the restart acceptance checklist and requirement to verify the stated minimum before full power application.
  - Append this ECN to the equipment file for EQ-P3-L1-IH03 and include cross-reference entries in the affected SOPs.

Approvals
- Engineering approval: Required before procedural changes are published and before control logic updates are implemented.
- Operations approval: Required for procedural acceptance and training closure for P3-L1 operators.
- Maintenance approval: Required for any control logic or hardware changes and for maintenance procedure updates.
- Document control: Upon approval, this ECN will be released to the controlled document system and referenced in SOP-P3-L1-02, SOP-P3-L1-03, and SOP-P3-L1-05.

Notes
- This ECN does not change any other equipment setpoints or introduce new hardware beyond required sensors or indicators to enforce and display the stated minimum. All implementation steps must be carried out in coordination with affected stakeholders and in accordance with applicable safety and lockout/tagout practices described in the referenced SOPs.
